page.layout: One page of running text in one column, no margin notes. The running head is above the text, the page number at the top right, the catchword at the bottom right and the gathering signature at the bottom left.

main_text.p: Respondemus I. τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ [?] hanc designari Epistolam, & quia, ut antè ostensum, scripta uni Galatarum Ecclesiae, & scripta Gentibus non Hebræis, & alius plane argumenti, de modo nempè nostrae justificationis coràm DEO. II. Illatio omninò inconsequens. Paulus juxta Petrum scripsit Hebræis sapientissimâ omninò ratione; Paulus in sua ad Galatas monet se edoctum divinitus, non ordinariè & mediatè ab hominibus, sed extraordinariè ac immediatè à Christo; Ergo Epistola illa ad Hebræos non alia fuerit ab eâ, quae est ad Galatas? Quasi verò Petrus non tam sublimitatem rerum, quàm verba illa de modo revelationis, attendat? Quasi sola ad Galatas, hoc nomine scripta dici debeat κατὰ τὴν δοθεῖσαν αὐτῷ σοφίαν [?]? Quasi Paulus in hac tantùm, non in aliis etiam ad Romanos, Corinthios, Thessalonicenses &c. Epistolis, à divinâ illâ & immediatâ origine doctrinam derivet suam? III. Est elenchus à dicto secundùm quid. Nec Paulus simpliciter scripsisse dicitur Petro secundùm datam sibi sapientiam, sed scri-psisse

page.notes: The running head reads "ad Hebræos." and the ligature in "Hebræos" is uncertain, so it is given as printed. The Greek at the start of the first line and the Greek in "κατὰ τὴν δοθεῖσαν αὐτῷ σοφίαν" are hard to read at this resolution and are marked [?]. The catchword at the bottom right is partly cut off and is read as "psisse" [?]. The page number "51" is read from a small, worn numeral. The paragraph is marked cont="true" because the page opens mid-argument at "Respondemus I." and no indent shows a new paragraph. No printing errors were corrected.
